name: IEC first-in first-out memory (FIFO)
summary: IEC element marked FIFO that stores words in arrival order and reads them out in the same order.
description: The FIFO qualifier identifies a first-in first-out memory. There are no address inputs; instead, a write clock stores input words and a read clock delivers them in the same order. Status outputs indicate empty, full and sometimes half-full conditions.

FIFOs buffer data between parts of a system that run at different rates, such as a serial receiver and a processor. On a drawing, the status outputs should be traced to see how the system avoids overflow and underflow.
The symbol does not specify depth or whether read and write clocks can be asynchronous. The organisation and device data provide those details.
readingNotes: No address inputs: order is implicit.
Trace full and empty flags to their handling logic.
drawingChecklist: Show status outputs and their use.
distinction: RAM uses addresses; FIFO uses order of arrival.
